frank_derived_assumptions.assumption: Replay/provenance-sensitive FRANK state needs stable semantic identity across source, typed IR, lowering and replay.
independent_support: RFC 8785 canonicalization exists specifically because hashes/signatures need invariant representations.
WebAssembly represents numeric types explicitly and encodes floating values by IEEE-754 bit patterns.
frank_derived_assumptions.note: External standards support deterministic typed representation as an engineering pattern, but do not validate FRANK's architecture or prove this exact ClayCode encoding.

frank_derived_assumptions.assumption: Canonical JSON can be used directly as universal numeric semantic identity.
independent_support: RFC 8785 restricts JSON numbers to IEEE-754 double, recommends strings for higher precision/longer integers, rejects NaN/Infinity and serializes negative zero as zero.
frank_derived_assumptions.note: JCS may remain valid for a deliberately restricted transport/contract layer.

frank_derived_assumptions.assumption: One deterministic binary encoding such as CBOR automatically resolves numeric semantics.
independent_support: RFC 8949 deterministic encoding still requires protocol-level choices about integer-versus-float identity, negative zero and special floating values.
frank_derived_assumptions.note: A wire canonicalizer is subordinate to the ClayCode typed semantic contract, not a replacement for it.

frank_derived_assumptions.assumption: Exact F64 bits are sufficient for all deterministic replay.
independent_support: WebAssembly encodes float bit patterns directly but arithmetic NaN results may admit multiple payload/sign outcomes.
frank_derived_assumptions.note: Literal/value identity and arithmetic semantic-equivalence classes must be distinguished.

strongest_counterhypothesis: Use an existing canonical format plus explicit string/tag wrappers for numbers, avoiding any Clay-specific numeric encoding beyond type metadata.
highest_information_test: Implement two production canonicalizers behind the same typed IR oracle: minimal Clay typed tokens versus standard deterministic CBOR/JCS-with-wrappers; compare semantic identity, diagnostics, implementation complexity, bytes, latency, replay stability and native/Wasm lowering on the same Ubuntu corpus.
anti_echo_boundary: Project worker results share ancestry and are not independent replication. Only external standards are treated as independent engineering analogues, not as validation of FRANK/Clay.
